## Overview
A global, cloud-native e-commerce platform delivering physical and electronic book sales, reviews, and personalized recommendations to 1 million monthly active users. It ensures high availability, strict security compliance, and sub-2-second global page loads.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Book Buyers, Registered Reviewers, Store Administrators
- **Core System**: Online Bookstore Web/Mobile Application
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal), Shipping Providers (UPS/FedEx/DHL), Tax & Compliance Service (Avalara/OneTrust), Identity Provider (AWS Cognito/Auth0), CDN / Edge WAF (Cloudflare/AWS CloudFront), Marketing & Email Service (SendGrid/Klaviyo), Observability & APM (Datadog/CloudWatch)

## Relationships
- **Users to CDN/WAF**: HTTPS (Web/Mobile traffic, TLS 1.3)
- **CDN/WAF to Core System**: Reverse proxy / DNS routing
- **Core System to Payment Gateway**: HTTPS / REST API
- **Core System to Shipping Providers**: Asynchronous event-driven queues / HTTPS REST API
- **Core System to Tax & Compliance Service**: HTTPS / REST API
- **Core System to Identity Provider**: HTTPS / OIDC / OAuth2
- **Core System to Marketing & Email Service**: HTTPS / REST API & Webhooks
- **Core System to Observability & APM**: HTTPS / OTLP

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Infrastructure**: AWS across *us-east-1*, *eu-west-1*, and *ap-southeast-1* for global multi-region redundancy.
- **Routing & Security**: Route 53 latency-based DNS, CloudFront/Cloudflare CDN, Edge WAF, and TLS 1.3 encryption-in-transit (AES-256 at-rest) to meet OWASP and privacy standards.
- **Authentication**: Managed Identity Provider (AWS Cognito/Auth0) utilizing OAuth2/OIDC with MFA for administrators.
- **Integration & Architecture**: Asynchronous event-driven queues to decouple third-party shipping and marketing services from core checkout, plus Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform/CDK).

## Rationale
This multi-region active-active architecture guarantees 99.95% availability and sub-2-second global performance by leveraging edge caching and latency-based DNS routing. Asynchronous decoupling isolates core checkout from third-party outages while meeting strict GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance requirements.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style online bookstore providing catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations for 1M MAU across three global AWS regions.]

## Key Elements
• Book Buyers, Registered Reviewers, Store Administrators
• React/Next.js SPA frontend in AWS S3 and CloudFront CDN
• AWS API Gateway for routing, rate-limiting, and JWT validation
• ECS Fargate containers: Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Recommendation, Pricing & Localization
• AWS RDS PostgreSQL, AWS OpenSearch, and AWS ElastiCache (Redis)
• AWS EventBridge/SNS-SQS for event-driven messaging
• External Systems: Payment Gateway, Shipping APIs, Tax & Compliance Service, Identity Provider

## Relationships
• Users to SPA via HTTPS/REST/GraphQL
• SPA to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST/GraphQL
• API Gateway to ECS Fargate containers via gRPC over HTTP/2 and mTLS
• Containers to RDS PostgreSQL and OpenSearch via TCP/TLS
• Containers to ElastiCache Redis via encrypted TCP
• Containers to AWS EventBridge/SNS-SQS via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
• React/Next.js: Chosen for high-performance SPA delivery via CDN
• Node.js/Go, Java/Spring Boot, Python/FastAPI: Polyglot backend optimized for search, ACID checkout, and recommendations
• AWS ECS Fargate: Standardized container orchestration ensuring zero-downtime deployments
• AWS RDS PostgreSQL: ACID-compliant relational storage with strict isolation for GDPR/CCPA
• AWS OpenSearch & ElastiCache: High-speed catalogue search and session/rate caching
• AWS Route 53 & CloudWatch: Global latency-based routing and centralized logging

## Rationale
[Standardized ECS Fargate containers combined with managed AWS services ensure 99.95% uptime, sub-second latency, and multi-region scalability for 1M MAU. Strict network isolation, encryption, and regional replication satisfy OWASP mitigations and GDPR/CCPA compliance.]

Frontend SPA.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style online bookstore offering physical and electronic books, search, cart, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations.]
[Engineered for global scalability, OWASP security compliance, and multi-currency transactions across three AWS regions.]

## Key Elements
• Book Buyers, Registered Reviewers, Store Administrators
• Frontend SPA (Next.js, React, AWS S3, CloudFront CDN)
• API Gateway (AWS API Gateway)
• Catalog & Search Service (ECS Fargate, Node.js/Go)
• Order & Checkout Service (ECS Fargate, Java/Spring Boot)
• Recommendation Service (ECS Fargate, Python/FastAPI)
• Pricing & Localization Service (ECS Fargate, Polyglot backend)
• Relational Database (AWS RDS PostgreSQL)
• Search Index (AWS OpenSearch)
• Cache & Session Store (AWS ElastiCache, Redis)
• Event Bus (AWS EventBridge, SNS, SQS)
• Catalog & Search UI Component, Cart & Checkout UI Component, Social Proof & Recommendation UI Component, Auth & Session Handler Component, Localization & Consent Manager Component

## Relationships
• Book Buyers, Registered Reviewers, Store Administrators -> Frontend SPA: Interacts with store interface [HTTPS, REST, GraphQL]
• Frontend SPA -> API Gateway: Sends API requests for catalogue, cart, and user actions [HTTPS, REST, GraphQL]
• API Gateway -> Backend Microservices (Catalog, Order, Recommendation, Pricing): Routes validated API traffic [gRPC, HTTPS]
• Backend Microservices -> Relational Database & Search Index: Persists data and queries search indexes [SQL, TLS]
• Frontend SPA -> AWS S3 / CloudFront CDN: Serves static assets and edge-cached pages [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
• Frontend Framework: Next.js and React for high-performance server-side rendering and client-side routing.
• Cloud Infrastructure: AWS S3 and CloudFront CDN with Lambda@Edge for low-latency global delivery (< 2s on 3G).
• Compute & Containers: AWS ECS Fargate for running microservices securely and scalably.
• Databases & Caching: AWS RDS PostgreSQL for transactional data, AWS OpenSearch for catalogue search, and AWS ElastiCache (Redis) for session management.
• Security & Integration: NextAuth.js / OAuth2, HttpOnly Secure cookies, and strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers for OWASP compliance.

## Rationale
[The Next.js and CloudFront edge architecture directly guarantees high performance under 3G constraints and 99.95% global availability across target AWS regions.]
[Containerized microservices on ECS Fargate paired with secure session handling ensure elastic scalability to 1M MAU while strictly enforcing GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP Top-10 security controls.]

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore API Gateway routes and secures all client interactions for catalogue browsing, secure checkout, and recommendations. It provides scalable, low-latency traffic management across three global AWS regions.

## Key Elements
- Edge Router & WAF Integration
- Authentication & Authorization Filter
- Rate Limiting & Throttling Engine
- Service-Discovery & Routing Proxy
- AWS API Gateway
- AWS WAF & CloudFront
- AWS ElastiCache (Redis)
- AWS ECS Fargate Microservices

## Relationships
- Frontend SPA -> Edge Router: Sends API requests for catalogue, checkout, and user actions [HTTPS, REST, GraphQL]
- Edge Router -> Auth Filter -> Throttling Engine -> Routing Proxy: Processes requests through an in-memory pipeline
- Routing Proxy -> ECS Fargate Microservices: Routes internal traffic [gRPC over HTTP/2, mTLS]
- Auth Filter & Throttling Engine -> AWS ElastiCache (Redis): Validates token blacklists and synchronizes distributed rate limits [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Manages unified routing, rate-limiting, and canary deployments
- AWS WAF & CloudFront: Enforces OWASP Top-10 mitigations, SSL termination, and schema validation
- AWS ElastiCache (Redis): Powers distributed rate limiting and JWT revocation lookups
- gRPC over HTTP/2 with mTLS: Ensures secure, low-latency internal service communication

## Rationale
This architecture decouples edge security, routing, and rate-limiting from backend microservices to handle 1 million MAU reliably. It guarantees high availability and meets strict security, privacy, and performance requirements.

Catalog & Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
- The Catalog & Search Service is a containerized microservice that powers high-speed, typo-tolerant book discovery, faceted browsing, and keyword search.
- It delivers sub-2-second search responses for 1M MAU while enforcing strict security, GDPR/CCPA compliance, and 99.95% availability.

## Key Elements
- **Search & Browse Router**: Node.js/Go component handling gRPC input validation and sanitization.
- **OpenSearch Query Builder**: Component translating domain queries into AWS OpenSearch DSL.
- **Ingestion & Indexing Worker**: Component consuming event bus updates for bulk index synchronization.
- **AWS OpenSearch**: Managed search index storing denormalized documents with localized pricing.
- **AWS RDS PostgreSQL**: Primary relational database for catalogue persistence.
- **AWS EventBridge / SQS**: Messaging infrastructure with Dead Letter Queues for sync events.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secure injection of database and search credentials.

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Search & Browse Router: Routes catalogue queries via gRPC over HTTP/2 with mTLS.
- Search & Browse Router -> OpenSearch Query Builder: Delegates parsed queries via in-memory function calls.
- OpenSearch Query Builder -> AWS OpenSearch: Executes search queries via HTTPS/TCP.
- Ingestion & Indexing Worker -> AWS OpenSearch: Bulk updates index documents via HTTPS/TCP.
- Event Bus -> Ingestion & Indexing Worker: Consumes catalogue change events via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js/Go**: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency gRPC request handling.
- **AWS OpenSearch**: Selected for scalable, typo-tolerant full-text search and faceted filtering.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Provides serverless container orchestration with horizontal autoscaling.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Ensures secure credential storage without plain-text exposure.

## Rationale
- Denormalizing localized prices directly into AWS OpenSearch eliminates runtime inter-service calls, ensuring sub-2-second performance.
- Private subnet isolation, IAM RBAC, and AWS KMS encryption meet strict security, GDPR/CCPA compliance, and uptime requirements.

Order & Checkout Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Order & Checkout Service is a cloud-native component of the Online Bookstore that handles ACID-compliant order processing, payment integration, and checkout orchestration. It ensures secure, resilient financial transactions across multiple global regions.

## Key Elements
- **Checkout Orchestrator Component**: Spring Boot / Spring State Machine managing distributed transaction sagas and idempotent API calls.
- **Order Management API Component**: Spring MVC/REST exposing secure endpoints for Customer Support Agent refunds and cancellations.
- **Order Persistence Component**: Spring Data JPA managing relational data against AWS RDS PostgreSQL.
- **Event Publisher Component**: Spring Cloud Stream / AWS SDK dispatching asynchronous events to AWS EventBridge.
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Tax & Compliance Service, and AWS Secrets Manager.

## Relationships
- Checkout Orchestrator -> Payment Gateway, Shipping APIs, Tax Service [HTTPS / REST API]
- Checkout Orchestrator -> Order Persistence Component [JPA/JDBC over TLS]
- Order Management API -> Order Persistence Component [JPA/JDBC over TLS]
- Checkout Orchestrator & Order Management API -> Event Publisher Component [In-process Spring Events]
- Event Publisher Component -> AWS EventBridge [HTTPS / AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- **Java / Spring Boot**: Chosen for enterprise maturity, robust transaction management, and ecosystem support.
- **AWS RDS PostgreSQL**: Provides strict ACID compliance and relational integrity for financial data.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Enables scalable, serverless container execution across multiple AWS regions.
- **AWS EventBridge / SQS**: Decouples domain event publishing (`OrderPlaced`, `AbandonedCheckout`) with dead-letter queue support.
- **AWS Secrets Manager & KMS**: Ensures zero hardcoded secrets and robust envelope encryption for PII at rest.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees 99.95% uptime and 1 M MAU scalability by decoupling core checkout sagas from downstream messaging via asynchronous event publishing. It strictly enforces PCI-DSS, GDPR, and OWASP security controls through zero credit card persistence, IAM least-privilege roles, and idempotency keys.

Recommendation Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore Recommendation Service provides personalized book suggestions and collaborative filtering to enhance user engagement. It leverages a Python FastAPI backend to deliver low-latency recommendations while maintaining strict GDPR and CCPA compliance.]

## Key Elements
- API Router (FastAPI)
- Recommendation Engine (Python, PyTorch/Scikit-learn runtime)
- Feature Store Client
- Cache Manager
- Experimentation & Telemetry Client
- AWS ElastiCache (Redis)
- AWS RDS PostgreSQL
- AWS EventBridge / SQS

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> API Router: Routes gRPC over HTTP/2 requests with mTLS
- Cache Manager -> AWS ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves cached recommendation data via Encrypted TCP
- Recommendation Engine -> AWS RDS PostgreSQL: Reads historical purchase graphs via SQL over TLS
- Experimentation & Telemetry Client -> AWS EventBridge / SQS: Publishes pseudonymized interaction events asynchronously

## Technology Stack
- Python with FastAPI: Chosen for high-performance asynchronous API routing and native integration with machine learning runtimes.
- PyTorch / Scikit-learn: Selected for executing collaborative filtering and "Customers also bought" models.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Utilized for isolated, scalable container execution with memory-optimized instances.
- AWS ElastiCache (Redis): Deployed to cache recommendation outputs and user context for sub-200ms response times.
- AWS KMS: Implemented for encrypting model artifacts at rest across multi-region deployments.

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples heavy machine learning inference from request routing to guarantee high availability and sub-200ms latency under peak loads. Strict data pseudonymization and resource isolation ensure compliance with privacy regulations while supporting scalable multi-region operations.]

Pricing & Localization Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore Pricing & Localization Service manages global multi-currency pricing, taxes, and localization rules across multiple AWS regions. It ensures high availability and sub-10ms performance to support secure international checkouts and compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Pricing API Controller**: Node.js/TypeScript (Fastify) component handling gRPC/HTTP requests.
- **Currency Exchange Engine**: Translates base prices into USD, EUR, and GBP using cached rates.
- **Localization Rule Resolver**: Fetches regional tax and compliance rules.
- **Price Cache Manager**: Manages caching logic and cache invalidation.
- **Exchange Rate Sync Worker**: Background worker fetching third-party currency rates.
- **Audit & Compliance Logger**: Captures administrative pricing updates.
- **AWS ElastiCache (Redis)**: Regional cache and session store with read-replicas.
- **AWS RDS PostgreSQL**: Relational database for persistent pricing and rules.
- **AWS EventBridge**: Pub/sub event bus for cache invalidation.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secure storage for external API credentials.

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Pricing API Controller: Routes localization requests [gRPC over HTTP/2, mTLS]
- Pricing API Controller -> Price Cache Manager: Reads localized pricing [Redis protocol over TCP/TLS]
- Price Cache Manager -> AWS ElastiCache: Populates and invalidates cache [TCP/TLS with Encryption at Rest/Transit]
- Localization Rule Resolver -> AWS RDS PostgreSQL: Fetches fallback rules on cache miss [TCP/TLS]
- AWS EventBridge -> Price Cache Manager: Triggers instant cache invalidation on admin updates [Pub/Sub]
- Exchange Rate Sync Worker -> AWS Secrets Manager: Retrieves API keys [IAM-authenticated task roles]

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js/TypeScript (Fastify)**: Powers the API controller and sync worker for low-latency handling.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Deploys containerized services across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`.
- **AWS ElastiCache (Redis)**: Provides sub-10ms localized pricing reads.
- **AWS RDS PostgreSQL**: Stores persistent pricing records and regional tax rules.
- **AWS EventBridge**: Facilitates real-time cache invalidation across regions.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secures third-party feed credentials.

## Rationale
Decomposing the service into localized ElastiCache layers and asynchronous workers ensures sub-10ms performance and 99.95% availability under high traffic. Multi-region deployments with secure secret management and fallback mechanisms satisfy strict global compliance and uninterrupted checkout requirements.

## Overview
The Search Index container provides high-performance, typo-tolerant catalogue search and near-real-time indexing for the Online Bookstore. It is architected to support 1M MAU, sub-second query responses, and global multi-region deployments while meeting strict security and compliance requirements.

## Key Elements
*   **Search Index (AWS OpenSearch):** Parent container providing distributed search and storage.
*   **Query Processor:** Component handling incoming search requests, typo-tolerance, analysis pipelines, and input sanitization.
*   **Indexing Engine:** Component consuming catalogue mutation events for near-real-time index updates.
*   **Cluster State & Storage:** Component managing primary-replica shards, EBS NVMe storage, and backup tiers across availability zones.
*   **Catalog & Search Service:** External container generating search queries.
*   **Event Bus (AWS SQS / EventBridge):** External messaging service delivering catalogue mutation events.

## Relationships
*   Catalog & Search Service -> Query Processor: HTTP/REST [TLS 1.3, AWS IAM SigV4]
*   Event Bus -> Indexing Engine: HTTP/REST [TLS 1.3, AWS IAM SigV4 via OpenSearch Bulk API]
*   Cluster State & Storage -> AWS S3: HTTPS [TLS 1.3 for Cross-Region Snapshots]

## Technology Stack
*   **AWS OpenSearch:** Distributed search engine providing multi-AZ sharding, cross-cluster replication, and 99.95% uptime.
*   **Lucene Analysis Pipeline:** Token filters, synonym mapping, and fuzzy-matching algorithms for search relevance.
*   **AWS IAM SigV4:** Zero-trust authentication enforcing strict service-to-service authorization.
*   **AWS KMS:** Customer Managed Keys (CMK) ensuring encryption-at-rest.
*   **AWS CloudWatch:** Monitoring, audit logging, and SIEM integration.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS OpenSearch with dedicated VPC isolation and IAM SigV4 to meet rigorous OWASP Top-10 security constraints and GDPR/CCPA compliance. Furthermore, the decoupling of the Query Processor and Indexing Engine with bulk API batching guarantees sub-second page loads and rapid catalog updates across all target regions.

## Overview
[The Online Bookstore system provides a scalable, secure, and compliant e-commerce platform for catalog browsing, ordering, and personalized recommendations. It guarantees high availability and sub-second performance for 1 million monthly active users globally across AWS regions.]

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Book Buyers, Registered Reviewers, Store Administrators
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway, Shipping Providers, Tax & Compliance Service, Identity Provider, CDN / Edge WAF, Marketing & Email Service, Observability & APM
- **Frontend Container**: Frontend SPA (React, Next.js, AWS S3, CloudFront CDN)
- **Backend Containers**: API Gateway (AWS API Gateway), Catalog & Search Service (ECS Fargate, Node.js/Go), Order & Checkout Service (ECS Fargate, Java/Spring Boot), Recommendation Service (ECS Fargate, Python/FastAPI), Pricing & Localization Service (ECS Fargate, Polyglot backend)
- **Data & Infrastructure Containers**: Relational Database (AWS RDS PostgreSQL), Search Index (AWS OpenSearch), Cache & Session Store (AWS ElastiCache (Redis)), Event Bus / Messaging (AWS EventBridge, SNS, SQS)
- **Cache Components**: Session Manager Component, Catalog & Pricing Cache Component, Rate Limiter & Throttle Component

## Relationships
- Frontend SPA -> CDN / Edge WAF: HTTPS
- API Gateway -> Order & Checkout Service: Encrypted HTTP/REST
- Order & Checkout Service -> Cache & Session Store (Session Manager): Encrypted TCP via Redis Protocol
- Catalog & Search Service -> Cache & Session Store (Catalog & Pricing Cache): Read/Write product details [Encrypted TCP via Redis Protocol]
- Pricing & Localization Service -> Cache & Session Store (Catalog & Pricing Cache): Read exchange rates [Encrypted TCP]
- API Gateway -> Cache & Session Store (Rate Limiter): Check rate limits [Encrypted TCP]

- **Compute**: AWS ECS Fargate for containerized microservices across multiple regions (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`)
- **Cache & Session**: AWS ElastiCache (Redis) configured with Cluster Mode, Multi-AZ, `volatile-lru` eviction, and Redis ACLs for segregated isolation
- **Database**: AWS RDS PostgreSQL with AWS KMS encryption at rest
- **Search**: AWS OpenSearch for catalog keyword search and recommendations
- **Security & Networking**: TLS 1.3 for encryption in transit, AWS Secrets Manager for Redis AUTH rotation, and AWS IAM / Security Groups for strict network boundaries

## Rationale
[This architecture leverages AWS managed services and a decomposed ElastiCache Redis topology to satisfy stringent performance, scalability, and security mandates. Strict component isolation, multi-region replication, and automated encryption ensure compliance with GDPR/CCPA while maintaining 99.95% uptime and sub-second page loads.]

Event Bus / Messaging.analysis:
## Overview
- Event-driven microservices architecture utilizing AWS serverless infrastructure to decouple services, ensure 99.95% uptime, and handle 1M MAU.
- Asynchronous messaging backbone for order processing, inventory syncing, and real-time recommendations while maintaining GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Event Router (AWS EventBridge):** Central event bus using JSON-based rules.
- **Notification Dispatcher (AWS SNS):** Pub/sub topic for broadcast notifications.
- **Order Queue (AWS SQS):** Durable, at-least-once processing queue with Dead Letter Queues (DLQs).
- **Analytics Stream (AWS Kinesis):** High-throughput clickstream and review event ingestion.
- **EventBridge Schema Registry:** JSON schema validation and contract enforcement.
- **Producers & Consumers:** Order & Checkout Service, Catalog & Search Service, Recommendation Service, Marketing & Email Service.

## Relationships
- **Order & Checkout Service -> Event Router:** Publishes `OrderPlaced` [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
- **Event Router -> Order Queue:** Routes `OrderPlaced` for downstream fulfillment [AWS Native]
- **Event Router -> Notification Dispatcher:** Broadcasts async triggers for emails [AWS Native]
- **Catalog & Search Service -> Event Router:** Publishes `ItemViewed` and `ReviewSubmitted` [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
- **Event Router -> Recommendation Service:** Streams engagement data asynchronously [AWS SQS / Kinesis]

## Technology Stack
- **AWS EventBridge:** Core event routing and schema registry for serverless scale and validation.
- **AWS SQS & SNS:** Reliable queuing, decoupling, and fan-out notifications.
- **AWS Kinesis:** High-throughput streaming for analytics and recommendations.
- **AWS KMS:** Customer-managed keys (CMK) for end-to-end data encryption and PII protection.
- **AWS IAM (SigV4):** Role-based authentication and least-privilege authorization.
- **AWS CloudWatch & X-Ray:** Distributed tracing, backpressure monitoring, and DLQ alarms.

## Rationale
- Serverless event-driven design decouples critical paths like checkout and recommendations to guarantee sub-2-second page loads and high availability.
- Built-in DLQs, AWS KMS encryption, and IAM controls directly satisfy rigorous security, disaster recovery, and GDPR/CCPA compliance constraints.
